---
title: "Web SDK reference"
description: "Initialization options, instance methods, and capture events."
---

For a working example, start with the [React quickstart](/external/web).

## createCapture(options)

Creates a capture instance and loads the scanner. Returns a promise that resolves to the instance. Initialize after your video element is mounted.

```javascript
import { createCapture } from '/bouncr/index.js';

const capture = await createCapture({
  video,
  token,
  configuration,
  onState,
});
```

### Required options

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `video` | `HTMLVideoElement` | Element used for the camera preview |
| `token` | `string` | Initialization token issued by your backend for this scan; initialize before it expires (up to 10 minutes) |
| `configuration` | `string` | Encoded configuration supplied by your backend for the same scan |
| `onState` | `(state: CaptureState) => void` | Called when capture state or guidance changes |

### Optional callbacks and options

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onCaptureComplete` | `(scanId: string) => void` | Required captures have been accepted |
| `onComplete` | `(scanId: string) => void` | Scan processing has finished |
| `onTorchChange` | `({ available, enabled }) => void` | Flashlight availability and state; both values are booleans |
| `onJobStatus` | Job-status callback | Additional processing progress for an advanced progress view |
| `onDiagnostics` | Diagnostics callback | Optional startup/frame timing data for troubleshooting |
| `maxAnalysisFps` | `number` | Analysis-rate ceiling; default `30` |

Keep callbacks short. Use [Handle results](/external/results) for application decisions and [Customize capture](/external/customize) for camera controls.

Your backend supplies `token` and `configuration` with your page or onboarding data. See [Connect your backend](/external/backend). To initialize a new instance after a refresh, obtain a fresh token for the same scan.

## Instance methods

### start(scanId?, documentType?, country?)

Starts or resumes capture. Returns `void`; progress arrives through `onState`.

```javascript
capture.start();
capture.start(existingScanId);
capture.start(existingScanId, undefined, 'US');
capture.start(existingScanId, DocumentType.DRIVERS_LICENSE, 'US');
```

For a new scan, the SDK requests a country and document selection. For an existing scan, it restores the selection and accepted captures. A permitted selection starts the camera when more images are needed.

### capture()

Requests manual capture using the current camera frame. Returns `void`. Available while capturing; the frame must satisfy the capture quality checks.

### stop()

Cancels the active capture and releases the camera. Returns `void`. Call `start()` to begin again with the same instance.

### destroy()

Releases the camera and SDK resources. Returns `void`. Call when leaving the page or unmounting the component. Create a new instance before starting again.

### setTorch(enabled)

Turns the active camera’s flashlight on or off. Returns `Promise<void>`. Rejects if the camera or flashlight is unavailable. Read availability through `onTorchChange`.

### setAnalysisFps(value)

Changes the analysis-rate ceiling. Returns `void`. Capture automatically adapts to the device’s processing time within this limit.

## CaptureState

<ResponseField name="phase" type="Phase value">
  Current stage
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="guidance" type="Guidance value">
  Current camera instruction
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="scanId" type="string, optional">
  ID for this scan
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="resumable" type="boolean">
  Accepted capture can be restored
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="countryCodes" type="string[]">
  Available issuing countries
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="country" type="string">
  Selected country; empty before selection
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="allowedDocumentTypes" type="DocumentType[] values">
  Document choices allowed for this selection
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="documentType" type="DocumentType value">
  Selected document
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="requiredSides" type="Side[] values">
  Requested capture sides
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="acceptedSides" type="Side[] values">
  Sides already accepted
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="givenName" type="string">
  Given name parsed from the submitted document after all required captures are accepted; empty when unavailable. Use it for an optional completion greeting. See [Handle results](/external/results#personalize-the-completion-message).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="error" type="{ code: ErrorCode, status: number }, optional">
  Failure details; status is `0` for a local SDK error
</ResponseField>

Use the exported enums to compare values. The SDK also exports `supportedDocumentTypes` for filtering document choices to the installed package’s capabilities.

### Phase values

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AUTHORIZING` | Requesting scan access |
| `SELECTING_DOCUMENT` | Waiting for country/document selection |
| `CAPTURING` | Camera capture is active |
| `SUBMITTING` | Uploading a captured image |
| `PROCESSING` | Waiting for scan processing |
| `COMPLETE` | Processing finished |
| `FAILED` | Capture could not continue; inspect `error` |
| `SUPERSEDED` | Another capture instance took over |
| `STOPPED` | Capture was canceled |

See [Troubleshooting](/external/recovery) for guidance and error recovery.

## Server helper

Import this helper in your backend:

```javascript
import { encodeConfiguration } from '@bouncr/capture/server';

const configuration = encodeConfiguration(apiUrl, scanId);
```

`apiUrl` is the integration’s API base URL. `scanId` is the scan created by your backend. The helper returns the string passed as `configuration` to `createCapture`.
